body:
Rapid repeated notes lose their gaps as the piano roll zooms out. Reserve a one-point core and a two-point gap while separate notes fit; otherwise draw the local run as a solid ribbon with uniform inset hatching. Diagonal marks repeat every six composition points, are 1.5 points thick, and dim the fill by 75%. The long edges remain continuous and sustained notes stay plain.

Grouping stays within the same source/channel/key, preserves resolvable rests and observation boundaries, and retains pitch bends and expressions. Recorded note times do not change. Texture follows take time without implying an exact attack count. Same-time onset tuning now also applies to minimum-length padding, removing the thin protruding line at the raw key pitch.

Independent correctness and design reviews found two edge cases, addressed here: an endpoint intensity step must not repaint the preceding pitch segment, and interleaved voices must retain onset paint order. Dense ribbons now split only their draw spans at interleaving boundaries, sharing geometry and hatch phase. The span selection includes antialiased end coverage. Design verdict: merge with these scoped adjustments; no follow-up issues or owner decisions required.

[Rendered examples at three zoom levels and 1×/2× density](docs/evidence/roll-density/README.md).

Validation: focused regressions reproduced the intensity and paint-order defects before their fixes. All 40 UI roll tests and UI Clippy pass. Existing GPU tests cover ornament coverage in all four orientations, and offline pixel tests cover six zoom/density cases with bloom. Final native Metal regeneration and complete CI are pending on the rebased branch.

Cloud handoff: `./build-pr.sh --load 1431`. Final release binaries and their verified overlay tag will be recorded after the validated Metal corpus is imported.
title: Keep piano-roll repeats legible as zoom changes
